g1_min_last_term_35.proof: PROVED MINIMAL. (1) For n=35 every bad prime p with 2p<=35 -- that is 2,5,11,17 -- must divide d: among 35 consecutive indices at least two terms are divisible by p, each needs p^2|, and their difference is p*j*d with j<p, forcing p|d. (2) 3|d is forced because a Loeschian number is never 2 mod 3. Hence d is a multiple of lcm(3,2,5,11,17)=5610. (3) Any 35-term AP with last term <= 311958331 has 34d <= 311958331, so d <= 9175245 and m = d/5610 <= 1635. (4) experiments/2026-10-03-g1opt swept ALL m = 1..1638 and ALL a with every term <= 311958331, and found exactly one 35-term AP: a=219830911, d=2709630. Therefore no 35-term Loeschian AP has a last term smaller than 311958331.
exhaustive_bounds: COMPLETE sweep m=1..1638 (covers every d with 34d <= 311958331), all a, all terms <= 311958331: exactly one 35-term AP exists, the record itself.
Earlier complete sweep to last term <= 2e8 found none (longest runs there are 27-29 terms).
